examples.en: Tomorrow is the first day of autumn, but it's still so hot.
Once ipchu passes, the breeze changes in the mornings and evenings.
According to the calendar, this year's ipchu is August 7.
Just because it's ipchu doesn't mean it suddenly gets cool.

examples.ko: 입추를 하루 앞두고 날씨가 푹푹 쪄요.
examples.en: The day before ipchu, the weather is sweltering.

examples.ko: 어제가 입추였는데 전혀 가을 같지 않았어요.
examples.en: Yesterday was ipchu, but it didn't feel like autumn at all.

explain: 달력으로는 가을이 시작되는 날이지만, 우리나라에서는 보통 아직 한창 더울 때예요. 다른 계절의 시작을 나타내는 '입춘', '입하', '입동'과 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: By the calendar it is the first day of autumn, but in Korea it is usually still the hottest part of summer. It helps to learn it together with 입춘, 입하 and 입동, which mark the start of the other seasons.

examples.en: How much is the gym's joining fee?
To join the club, you have to pay a joining fee.

examples.ko: 입회비는 처음에 한 번만 내면 돼요.
examples.en: You only have to pay the joining fee once at the beginning.

examples.ko: 입회비 삼만 원과 월회비 만 원을 냈어요.
examples.en: I paid a 30,000 won joining fee and a 10,000 won monthly fee.
There's an event where they discount the joining fee.
I paid the joining fee and got my membership card too.

explain: 모임이나 동호회, 운동 시설에 처음 들어갈 때 한 번 내는 돈이에요. 매달 내는 '월회비', 매년 내는 '연회비'와 구별해서 쓰고, '가입비'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is the one-time money you pay when first joining a club, group or gym. Do not confuse it with 월회비 (monthly fee) or 연회비 (annual fee), and people also say 가입비.

en: join; attach; put side by side

examples.ko: 짧은 줄 두 개를 잇대서 길게 만들었어요.
examples.en: I joined two short strings together to make a long one.

examples.ko: 책상 두 개를 잇대어 놓으니 넓어졌어요.
examples.en: When I put two desks side by side, it became wider.

examples.ko: 모자란 부분에 다른 천을 잇대 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried joining another piece of cloth onto the short part.
I joined the boards together and nailed them.

examples.ko: 종이를 잇대면 더 큰 포스터가 돼요.
examples.en: If you join the papers together, it becomes a bigger poster.
I placed the bookshelf by setting it right against the wall.

explain: 무언가의 끝이나 옆에 다른 것을 바짝 붙여서 이어지게 하는 느낌이에요. 말할 때는 '이어 붙이다'처럼 풀어서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It gives the feeling of placing something right up against the end or side of another thing so that they connect. In speech people also say it more plainly as '이어 붙이다'.

examples.ko: 친구 집에서 잉꼬 두 마리를 키워요.
examples.en: My friend keeps two parakeets at home.

examples.ko: 잉꼬가 제 말을 따라 해서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The parakeet copied what I said and I was startled.

examples.ko: 잉꼬 새장을 햇볕 드는 곳에 두었어요.
examples.en: I put the parakeet cage where the sun comes in.
That couple is a well-known loving couple in the neighborhood.

examples.ko: 잉꼬한테 먹이를 주는 게 제 아침 일과예요.
examples.en: Feeding the parakeet is my morning routine.

examples.ko: 잉꼬도 앵무새처럼 말을 배울 수 있나요?
examples.en: Can a parakeet learn to talk like a parrot too?

explain: 작고 알록달록한 새로, 집에서 많이 키워요. 새 이름보다 사이좋은 부부를 가리키는 '잉꼬부부'로 더 자주 들어요. 이 표현은 칭찬이에요.

phrases.en: You two really seem like a loving couple.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 이야기가 아니라 금실 좋은 부부를 가리켜요. 보통 칭찬으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is not about birds but about a couple with a very close relationship, usually said as a compliment.

explain_en: It is a small, colorful bird often kept at home. You hear it more often in '잉꼬부부', which refers to a couple who get along very well. That expression is a compliment.

examples.en: The baby has been whimpering since a while ago, probably sleepy.
Don't whine, try saying it in words.

examples.ko: 동생이 사 달라고 잉잉거리면 정말 힘들어요.
examples.en: It's really hard when my little brother whines to buy him something.
The puppy is whimpering in front of the door.
I don't know why he's whining since morning.
The child kept whining, so it was hard to feed him.

explain: 아이나 강아지가 울먹이며 보채는 소리를 낼 때 써요. '칭얼거리다'와 비슷한데, 어른이 이렇게 하면 놀리거나 나무라는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is used when a child or a puppy makes a fussy, tearful sound to get attention. It is similar to '칭얼거리다', and said about an adult it sounds teasing or scolding.

examples.en: There is a mother-of-pearl wardrobe in my grandmother's room.
This mirror's frame is decorated with mother-of-pearl.

examples.ko: 자개가 빛에 따라 색이 다르게 보여요.
examples.en: The mother-of-pearl looks like a different color depending on the light.
I received a small mother-of-pearl table as a gift.
Mother-of-pearl wardrobes are still regarded as high-end furniture.

examples.ko: 전통 공예 박물관에서 자개 작품을 구경했어요.
examples.en: I looked at mother-of-pearl works at the traditional craft museum.

explain: 조개껍데기 안쪽의 반짝이는 부분을 얇게 잘라 가구나 상자에 붙여 꾸밀 때 쓰는 재료예요. '자개장', '자개상'처럼 가구 이름 앞에 붙여 많이 말하고, 이런 공예를 '나전칠기'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is the shiny inner part of a shell, cut thin and attached to furniture or boxes as decoration. It is often placed before furniture names such as 자개장 and 자개상, and this craft is also called 나전칠기.

examples.ko: 그 말은 자격지심 때문에 더 아프게 들렸어요.
examples.en: Because of my own insecurity, those words hurt even more.
I used to feel inferior because of my educational background.

examples.ko: 괜히 자격지심에 그 모임에 가기 싫었어요.
examples.en: For no good reason, I felt insecure and didn't want to go to that gathering.

examples.ko: 자격지심 좀 버리고 당당하게 말해 보세요.
examples.en: Let go of your insecurity a bit and speak confidently.
He always compares himself to others out of insecurity.

examples.ko: 자격지심이 심해서 사진 찍는 걸 피해요.
examples.en: I'm so self-conscious that I avoid being photographed.

explain: 스스로 부족하다고 느끼는 마음 때문에, 남이 하는 말이나 행동을 괜히 나쁘게 받아들일 때 써요. 영어의 'guilty conscience'보다는 '열등감'에 가깝고, '자격지심이 있다/들다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when feeling inadequate makes you take other people's words or actions the wrong way. It is closer to an inferiority complex than to the English 'guilty conscience', and is used as '자격지심이 있다/들다'.

examples.ko: 자고로 사람은 약속을 잘 지켜야 해요.
examples.en: As they say, a person should keep their promises.

examples.ko: 자고로 음식은 제철에 먹는 게 최고예요.
examples.en: They say food is best eaten in season.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 자고로 어른 말씀은 들어야 한다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: Grandfather said that, as has always been the case, you should listen to your elders.

examples.ko: 옛말에 자고로 가는 말이 고와야 오는 말이 곱다고 했어요.
examples.en: The old saying goes that kind words get kind words in return.

examples.ko: 자고로 친구는 어려울 때 알아본다고 해요.
examples.en: They say you know who your real friends are in hard times.

examples.ko: 어머니는 자고로 집은 햇볕이 잘 들어야 좋다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: Mother said a house should get plenty of sunlight.

explain: 예로부터 그래 왔다고 말하면서 옛 이치나 교훈을 꺼낼 때 써요. 어르신들의 말투에서 많이 들리고, 뒤에는 '~다고 해요', '~는 법이에요'가 자주 와요.
explain_en: It is used to bring up an old principle or lesson, as in 'it has always been so'. You often hear it in the speech of older people, and it is often followed by endings such as '~다고 해요' or '~는 법이에요'.

examples.ko: 회사가 적자를 줄이기 위한 자구책을 내놓았어요.
examples.en: The company came up with a self-help plan to reduce its deficit.

examples.ko: 가게 문을 닫기 전에 자구책부터 찾아봐야 해요.
examples.en: Before closing the shop, we should look for a way to help ourselves.

examples.ko: 정부만 기다릴 수 없어서 우리 스스로 자구책을 마련했어요.
examples.en: We couldn't just wait for the government, so we prepared our own measures.
It will be hard to solve the problem with this measure alone.

examples.ko: 학교는 학생 수 감소에 대한 자구책 마련에 나섰어요.
examples.en: The school started preparing its own measures against the decline in students.
I'm not sure whether that measure will work.

explain: 남이 도와주기를 기다리지 않고 스스로 어려움에서 벗어나려는 방법을 말해요. 뉴스에서 회사나 기관의 어려운 상황을 이야기할 때 '자구책을 마련하다/내놓다'로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to a method of getting out of difficulty by your own effort instead of waiting for help. In the news it often appears as '자구책을 마련하다/내놓다' when companies or organizations are in trouble.

examples.en: I put a small flowerpot by the window.
That shop is small, but it's really neat.
The baby's hands are so tiny that they're cute.

examples.ko: 방이 자그마니까 가구를 많이 못 놓아요.
examples.en: The room is small, so I can't put much furniture in.
I answered in a small voice.
I want to live in a house that's small but cozy.

explain: '조그맣다'와 비슷하게 작고 아담한 것을 말하는데, 귀엽거나 소박한 느낌이 들어요. 'ㅎ' 불규칙이라서 '자그매요', '자그마니까', '자그만 집'처럼 바뀌어요.
explain_en: Like '조그맣다', it describes something small and compact, often with a cute or modest feel. It is an ㅎ-irregular, so it changes as in '자그매요', '자그마니까' and '자그만 집'.

examples.ko: 친구의 성공이 저에게 좋은 자극제가 됐어요.
examples.en: My friend's success became a good stimulus for me.
Coffee seems like a stimulant that drives away sleepiness.
This failure actually worked as a spur for me.

examples.ko: 자극제가 필요할 때는 새로운 취미를 시작해 보세요.
examples.en: When you need a boost, try starting a new hobby.
Friendly competition is a motivator for each other.
One comment from my senior was a big motivation to me.

explain: 약처럼 몸을 자극하는 것도 가리키지만, 일상에서는 의욕을 불러일으키는 계기라는 비유로 더 많이 써요. '친구의 성공이 자극제가 됐다'처럼 '자극제가 되다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It can mean something that stimulates the body like a drug, but in daily life it is more often used figuratively for something that sparks motivation, as in '친구의 성공이 자극제가 됐다'. It is used as '자극제가 되다'.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 자금력이 탄탄해서 걱정이 없어요.
examples.en: That company has solid financial strength, so there's nothing to worry about.
Big companies expand the market by leading with their financial power.
I'm looking for an investor with financial resources.
We fall behind our competitors in funding power.

examples.ko: 자금력만으로는 좋은 제품을 만들 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't make a good product with funding power alone.
Funding is important, but ideas are more important.

explain: 사업이나 일을 하는 데 필요한 돈을 마련하고 쓸 수 있는 힘이에요. 비슷한 '자본력'은 회사나 사업의 밑천을, '재력'은 주로 개인의 재산을 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It is the ability to raise and spend the money needed for a business or project. The similar word '자본력' stresses the capital of a company or business, while '재력' is mainly used for an individual's wealth.

examples.en: Saying you're fine is nothing but self-deception.
I think that's self-deception.

examples.ko: 자기기만에서 벗어나야 문제를 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to get out of self-deception to see the problem.

examples.ko: 실패를 남 탓으로만 돌리는 것도 자기기만이에요.
examples.en: Blaming others for every failure is also self-deception.
If you fall into self-deception, it's hard to see reality.
He stopped fooling himself and told the truth honestly.

explain: 남이 아니라 자기 자신을 속이는 것이고, '자기기만에 빠지다'처럼 자주 써요. 핑계를 대며 스스로를 정당화하는 느낌일 때는 '자기합리화'와 가깝게 쓰이기도 해요.
explain_en: It means deceiving yourself rather than other people, and is often used as '자기기만에 빠지다'. When it has the feeling of making excuses to justify yourself, it comes close to '자기합리화'.

examples.ko: 그는 자기도취에 빠져 남의 말을 안 들어요.
examples.en: He is lost in self-admiration and doesn't listen to others.
Isn't it self-infatuation to just keep looking in the mirror?
It's hard to work with someone who is extremely self-absorbed.
The lyrics of this song are too self-absorbed.

examples.ko: 자기도취도 적당하면 자신감이 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Self-admiration in moderation can become confidence.

examples.ko: 사진을 올릴 때 자기도취일까 봐 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I worry that posting photos might look self-obsessed.

explain: 자기 자신이 멋지고 대단하다고 여기며 푹 빠져 있는 모습을 말하고, 대개 부정적으로 써요. '나르시시즘'이라는 외래어도 있지만 일상 대화에서는 '자기도취에 빠졌다'처럼 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It describes being deeply absorbed in thinking you yourself are wonderful, and it is usually negative. The loanword '나르시시즘' also exists, but in conversation people often say things like '자기도취에 빠졌다'.

examples.en: If your words and actions differ, it's a contradiction.
I also realized my own contradiction while speaking.
That argument is caught in self-contradiction.
Writing with self-contradictions is uncomfortable to read.
It looks like a contradiction, but there's actually a reason.

examples.ko: 다이어트한다며 야식을 먹는 건 자기모순 아닐까요?
examples.en: Isn't eating late-night snacks while saying you're on a diet a contradiction?

explain: 자기가 한 말이나 생각, 행동이 서로 맞지 않는 상황에 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '앞뒤가 안 맞다'라고도 하고, 글이나 토론에서는 '자기모순'이라고 짚어 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is used when a person's own words, thoughts or actions do not match each other. In daily talk people also say '앞뒤가 안 맞다', while in writing and debate people often point it out as '자기모순'.

examples.en: Healthy self-love is helpful in life.
He has a strong self-love, so he likes compliments.
To grow your self-love, try praising yourself.
Self-love and selfishness are different.
My self-love weakened a lot after I got hurt.

examples.ko: 요즘 자기애에 관한 책을 읽고 있어요.
examples.en: These days I'm reading a book about self-love.

explain: 자기를 아끼고 사랑하는 마음이라서 좋은 뜻으로 쓰기도 하고, 지나치게 자기만 생각하는 모습을 말할 때는 부정적으로 쓰기도 해요. 앞뒤 말을 보고 판단해야 하고, '자존감'은 스스로를 가치 있게 여기는 마음이라 조금 달라요.
explain_en: It means caring about and loving yourself, so it can be positive, but it can also be negative when describing someone who thinks too much about themselves. Judge by the context, and note that '자존감' (self-esteem) is a little different.

examples.ko: 우리 아버지는 자린고비라서 불을 항상 꺼요.
examples.en: My father is a penny pincher, so he always turns off the lights.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 자린고비 소리를 들어도 신경 안 써요.
examples.en: That friend doesn't care even when called a miser.

examples.ko: 자린고비처럼 아끼기만 하지 말고 가끔은 쓰세요.
examples.en: Don't just save like a miser, spend sometimes.

examples.ko: 자린고비 같은 사장님이 월급을 올려 주실까요?
examples.en: Would a boss who's as tight as a miser raise our pay?

examples.ko: 누가 자린고비 아니랄까 봐 영수증까지 챙기네요.
examples.en: True to being a skinflint, he even keeps the receipt.

examples.ko: 저는 자린고비는 아니지만 아껴 쓰는 편이에요.
examples.en: I'm not a miser, but I tend to be thrifty.

explain: 돈을 너무 아끼는 사람을 놀리듯이 부르는 말이에요. '구두쇠', '짠돌이'와 비슷하고, 가까운 사이에서 농담처럼 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is a teasing name for a person who is too stingy with money. It is similar to '구두쇠' and '짠돌이', and is often used jokingly between people who are close.

examples.ko: 아이의 자립심을 키우려면 혼자 해 보게 하세요.
examples.en: To build a child's independence, let them try things alone.
I moved out early, so I became more self-reliant.

examples.ko: 자립심 있는 청년이 되도록 가르치고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to teach them to become self-reliant young people.
Independence starts with small things.
I learned self-reliance by traveling alone.
After living alone, my sense of independence grew too.

explain: 남에게 기대지 않고 스스로 해 나가려는 마음이에요. '자립심을 기르다/키우다'처럼 많이 말하고, 아이 교육이나 독립 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the mind-set of trying to manage on your own without leaning on others. It is often said as '자립심을 기르다/키우다' and appears a lot in talk about raising children or becoming independent.

examples.en: If you fall into conceit, it's easy to make mistakes.

examples.ko: 한 번 이겼다고 자만심을 가지면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't get conceited just because you won once.
His arrogance damaged the teamwork.
Conceit gets in the way of growth.
Because of my conceit, I ignored the advice.
I want to learn humility instead of conceit.

explain: '자신감'은 좋은 뜻이지만 '자만심'은 자기가 잘났다고 지나치게 믿는 마음이라 나쁘게 들려요. 반대말은 '겸손'이고, 같은 뜻의 동사는 '자만하다'예요.
explain_en: '자신감' (confidence) is positive, but '자만심' is an excessive belief that you are great, so it sounds negative. The opposite is '겸손' (humility), and the related verb is '자만하다'.

examples.en: I tried asking and answering questions to myself alone in my room.
He prepared for the interview by asking and answering questions himself.
It was a speech where the speaker asked questions and answered them himself.
When you're worried, asking and answering yourself helps organize your thoughts.
When no one answered, he ended up answering his own question.
As I asked and answered myself, the answer became clear.

explain: 스스로 묻고 스스로 대답한다는 점에서 그냥 혼잣말을 하는 것과 달라요. 고민을 정리할 때도 쓰고, 발표나 글에서 질문을 던진 뒤 직접 답하는 방식을 가리키기도 해요.
